summary: The petition challenged the implementation of the One Rank One Pension (OROP) policy by the Union Government, arguing that the revised definition—replacing automatic pension revision with periodic revision every five years—violated the original principle of OROP and was arbitrary and unconstitutional under Articles 14 and 21. The petitioners contended that OROP, as recommended by the Koshyari Committee and accepted in principle by the government in 2014, required automatic passing on of pension increases to past pensioners. The government's 2015 notification, however, introduced periodic revisions, leading to claims of discriminatory treatment and breach of assurance. The Court examined the factual background, submissions, and constitutional implications.
final_judgment: The Court upheld the petitioners' contention that the implementation of OROP must adhere to the principle of automatic revision to ensure equality and justice, directing the Union Government to revisit the method of revision to ensure it aligns with constitutional principles and prior assurances.
